key.decision_why: The author answered laurynmm's reachability question with a reworked two-commit push, and no reviewer was assigned before the comment, so a triager needs to see this; the change answers the feedback rather than replacing the PR, so a note is enough.
key.action_why: On 2026-07-20 laurynmm removed "not ready", added "maintainer review" and assigned karlstolley to confirm the cleanups.
changed: Answered where each of the four selectors can appear in the web app, splitting them into reachable and unreachable.
Removed the two unreachable selectors, `.alert-box .stacktrace` and `.alert.alert-danger`, in a separate commit with the reasoning in the description.
Merged the two remaining rules (`.alert-box .alert` and `.alert.alert-error`) in a second commit, keeping `.alert-box .alert` for the generic_embed_error banner.
Redid the verification on real app elements (`#home-error` and the generic_embed_error banner), with computed styles identical on main and the branch in both themes.
Added a check that `.alert-box .blueslip-error-container` is null, as evidence the stacktrace selector is dead.
still_missing: There are no precise before/after screenshots in light and dark theme, which the issue asks cleanup PRs to include; the author offers computed-style numbers instead.
No maintainer has yet confirmed that the two removed selectors are really unreachable.
key.reply_ask: Thank the author and say the PR is moving to maintainer review, where a CSS maintainer will confirm the dead-selector removals.

must_have.fact: Says the author answered the feedback by showing which selectors are reachable and removing the two dead ones, `.alert-box .stacktrace` and `.alert.alert-danger`.
Recommends handing off: remove "not ready" and add "maintainer review".
Names karlstolley, the CSS maintainer who opened #39354, as the reviewer.
Notes that the verification is computed-style measurements on the real `#home-error` and generic_embed_error elements rather than the precise before/after screenshots the issue asks for.
